evidence.positive: On demo-demo, created a patient with an MRSA_INFECTION observation 'MRSA Positive' dated 1 day ago and a case for p-elective-cerebrospinal-fluid-shunting (configured 'CEFAZOLIN -> VANCOMYCIN -> CLINDAMYCIN'). GET /api/admin/patients/{pmrn}/operations/{caseId}/antibiotic-candidates returned outcome RECOMMENDED with a single option {CEFAZOLIN, VANCOMYCIN}, mrsaAdjusted:true, while the pathway's own step 2 VANCOMYCIN stayed NOT_SELECTED. POST /api/cds/medication-selection with m-vancomycin-iv returned only w-dose-option-adjustment; the not-fired record for a-known-procedure-wrong-antibiotic reads 'Selected medication is a preferred antibiotic candidate' (app log: 'Rule evaluated: a-known-procedure-wrong-antibiotic -> false Selected medication is a preferred antibiotic candidate'). Firing PROCEDURE_START via /api/admin/events/category-event on an MRSA-positive case produced an a-incomplete-antibiotic-pathway fired result with PATHWAY_STATUS NONE_GIVEN, MRSA_ADJUSTED_OPTION_RECOMMENDED true and ANTIBIOTIC_GROUPS [[CeFAZolin, Vancomycin]]; on a second MRSA-positive case with cefazolin given through /api/admin/bolus first, the same event produced PARTIALLY_GIVEN with medsAdministered [CeFAZolin] and missingMeds [Vancomycin]. p-appendectomy ('CEFAZOLIN AND METRONIDAZOLE -> ...') resolved to {CEFAZOLIN, METRONIDAZOLE, VANCOMYCIN} mrsaAdjusted:true and vancomycin selection abstained. With a vancomycin anaphylaxis allergy the case resolved to {CEFAZOLIN, DAPTOMYCIN} and {CEFAZOLIN, LINEZOLID} (contraindicated [VANCOMYCIN]), daptomycin selection fired nothing; with vancomycin plus linezolid allergies only {CEFAZOLIN, DAPTOMYCIN} remained; with all three allergic the outcome was ALL_CONTRAINDICATED with recommended [].
evidence.negative: Same procedure, same calls, four patients that are not MRSA positive: no MRSA observation at all; 'MRSA Positive' 3 days ago followed by 'MRSA Negative' 1 day ago; 'MRSA Positive' 9 days ago (outside the 7-day window); and an unreadable value 'Pending'. Each resolved to {CEFAZOLIN} only with mrsaAdjusted:false, and selecting m-vancomycin-iv fired a-known-procedure-wrong-antibiotic with MRSA_ADJUSTED_OPTION_RECOMMENDED false. A non-MRSA case given cefazolin then PROCEDURE_START produced no a-incomplete-antibiotic-pathway alert (not-fired: 'Procedure candidates were given.'). MRSA-positive patients whose step 1 is not exactly cefazolin or cefazolin+metronidazole were left as configured: p-ent-clean-placement-of-prosthesis ('CEFAZOLIN OR CEFUROXIME') resolved to {CEFAZOLIN} and {CEFUROXIME}, p-clean-with-entry-into-urinary-tract ('(CEFAZOLIN AND GENTAMICIN) OR CEFAZOLIN') to {CEFAZOLIN, GENTAMICIN} and {CEFAZOLIN}, both mrsaAdjusted:false, and selecting vancomycin or daptomycin fired the wrong-antibiotic alert on both. On the cefazolin+metronidazole MRSA case, selecting daptomycin (not offered because vancomycin was safe) still fired the wrong-antibiotic alert.
evidence.red_check: Two red checks. (1) Pre-fix code: extracted ProcedureAntibioticCandidateService.java from the parent commit d27babc77, replaced @Slf4j with an explicit LoggerFactory logger, compiled it inside the app container with javac against /app/jib-classpath-file, backed up the six shipped ProcedureAntibioticCandidateService*.class files (sha256 recorded in scratch/shipped.sha256), copied the pre-fix classes over /app/classes and restarted the container (Started OrciApplication at 20:36:34Z). A fresh MRSA-positive case on the same procedure then resolved to {CEFAZOLIN} only, mrsaAdjusted:false; selecting m-vancomycin-iv fired a-known-procedure-wrong-antibiotic (the ticket's reported bug), and PROCEDURE_START produced NONE_GIVEN with ANTIBIOTIC_GROUPS [[CeFAZolin]] and MRSA flag false. Restored the backed-up classes, verified sha256 of every restored file matched the shipped checksums, restarted again (Started OrciApplication at 20:37:26Z), and re-ran: a fresh MRSA-positive case resolved to {CEFAZOLIN, VANCOMYCIN} mrsaAdjusted:true, vancomycin abstained, and PROCEDURE_START listed [CeFAZolin, Vancomycin] again. (2) Data flip on a fresh MRSA-positive case: vancomycin abstained; added a later 'MRSA Negative' observation, re-read candidates (now {CEFAZOLIN} only) and vancomycin selection fired the wrong-antibiotic alert; deleted the observations, re-added the positive, and vancomycin abstained again ('-> false Selected medication is a preferred antibiotic candidate').

caveats: Validated only on the demo tenant through admin APIs and the medication-selection API; the alert text and the added MRSA citation on the two alerts were not rendered in the browser UI (MRSA_ADJUSTED_OPTION_RECOMMENDED in the fired details confirms the conditional-citation branch is taken, but citations are not exposed by the evaluation endpoints used).

Cases were admin-created and never passed through app launch; MRSA status was read when the resolution was first computed and the 24h Redis resolution cache then held it, which matches the ticket's 'read once' intent but means a later result is picked up whenever that cache is dropped (allergy or procedure change) or expires.

Pre-existing quirk unrelated to this ticket: the admin antibiotic-candidates debug endpoint drops the cached resolution after its own transaction commits, so its first read after a data change still shows the previous answer and only the next read re-resolves.
Vancomycin being 'ruled out' was staged via TYPE_I medication allergies (a-general-allergy); other FILTERS_ANTIBIOTIC_CANDIDATES rules that could rule out vancomycin were not exercised.

The linezolid ANTIBIOTIC-category constraint was checked statically: at the built SHA the demo, MGB and Mayo master medication lists all carry LINEZOLID | ANTIBIOTIC, not exercised at runtime for MGB or Mayo.

automation.assessment: Backend coverage shipped with the PR is strong: MrsaAdjustedResolutionSpecTest (24 tests, the spec table incl. vancomycin/daptomycin/linezolid fallbacks and non-matching step 1s), MrsaStatusServiceTest (reading and 7-day/later-negative logic), and rule-level tests for both alerts. qa-suite has no MRSA end-to-end coverage at all (the only MRSA reference is a Mayo FHIR command spec); procedure-antibiotics.spec.ts (PABX, next free PABX-021) already exercises the resolution via the admin antibiotic-candidates endpoint and patient-api.ts already has addObservation, so the wiring from observation to resolution to both alerts is cheap to lock in as supplemental tests.

jira_comment:
Verdict: deploy-ready.

Positive: An MRSA-positive patient on a cefazolin pathway resolved to cefazolin plus vancomycin, selecting vancomycin raised no wrong-antibiotic alert, and procedure start asked for both drugs or for the missing vancomycin when only cefazolin was given.
Negative: Patients with no result, a later negative, a result older than 7 days, or a non-matching step 1 kept the configured pathway and vancomycin was still flagged, while a vancomycin allergy swapped in daptomycin or linezolid and all three allergic gave no recommendation.
Red check: Swapping the pre-fix resolution class into the running container made the MRSA-positive patient get cefazolin alone and vancomycin flagged wrong, and restoring the shipped class brought the fix back.

Automation: Backend tests shipped with the PR cover the spec table, and five supplemental PABX end-to-end tests are proposed to lock in the observation-to-alert wiring.
